transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood Solutions), Nora Patel (Redwood Product), Martin Lowe (VentraCloud PM), Sofia Ruiz (VentraCloud SE), Daniel O'Neal (VentraCloud Marketplace Ops), Aisha Khan (VentraCloud Security)

Summary Note (auto): Align on artifacts and timeline for VentraCloud marketplace listing and reference architecture for private VPC offering.

[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'll hand it over quick to Martin to say hi from VentraCloud side then we'll jump into the agenda
[00:12] Martin Lowe: thanks Alex, hi all, Martin here, uh excited to align on the joint solution, we want to make sure the marketplace listing covers both hosted and our managed private offering
[00:25] Priya Rao: great, quick context from the Redwood side - SE perspective: we typically provide a reference architecture for VPC/private, a marketplace listing payload, and a small runbook for initial onboarding and perf benchmarks
[00:40] Sofia Ruiz: quick question - for the private deployment, do you require a full on-prem bundle or is it ok to have customer-managed VPC with connector?
[00:52] Priya Rao: good q - our usual pattern is customer-managed VPC with the Redwood Private control plane in partner tenancy, or in some customers we ship an on-prem package for air-gapped. for VentraCloud we discussed earlier a VPC-stack with our connector and optional on-prem agent for regulated customers
[01:12] Daniel O'Neal: from marketplace ops perspective, we need the listing metadata, thumbnails, a short 1-2 page quickstart and the vendor contact email. also need to know if there are any special pricing models (reserved vs usage) to show in the listing
[01:30] Alex Kim: yep we'll provide a listing draft. action: Alex will share the draft marketplace listing plus screenshots and an artifact checklist.
[01:39] Aisha Khan: security folks here - we need to validate KMS integration and audit log availability, also data residency statements. do you have SOC 2 or ISO docs we can reference?
[01:50] Nora Patel: yes Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, we can share the security pack. we'll also annotate what parts of the solution require customer-managed KMS versus Redwood-managed keys for the test/pilot
[02:05] Martin Lowe: perfect. i'd like to sketch the reference arch now - can we run through a high-level topology?
[02:12] Priya Rao: sure i'll share my screen - um (screen sharing noise) so at a high level, VentraCloud VPC sits on the left, we provision a connector subnet that allows egress to Redwood control plane endpoints, the inference plane (gpu pools) can be in Redwood or dedicated partner-managed nodes depending on the agreement. the KV cache and prefix caching happen local to the inference nodes to keep latency low
[02:42] Sofia Ruiz: you said KV cache - are there compatibility notes for our managed redis versus in-memory KV?
[02:52] Priya Rao: we support both but recommend the in-memory local caching for latency sensitive flows; for larger multi-tenant setups redis can be used, we have some config knobs, we'll share the recommended config in the runbook
[03:10] Martin Lowe: latency/cost tradeoffs are important - on our marketplace some customers will want low latency for chat and others will prefer cheaper batch for embeddings. how are we thinking about routing policies and fallbacks?
[03:26] Liam Chen: Redwood runtime supports policy-based routing; you can route by cost, latency, or region. typical joint solution is to expose those as knobs in the marketplace listing and highlight the default profile: low-latency, balanced, cost-optimized. also mention automatic fallbacks to quantized variants when capacity constrained
[03:48] Daniel O'Neal: do you have benchmark numbers we can show? even rough P95 latency for 2k token chat on a dedicated pool would be helpful
[03:58] Priya Rao: we have internal perf sheets; for dedicated A100 pools p95 for 2k token chat is around 180-220ms per token in optimized paths but for the listing we'd likely show typical end-to-end times per request, not per token - we'll run a smoke test and share numbers
[04:20] Alex Kim: action item for Priya to run a reference-arch smoke test with VentraCloud network settings and upload the perf snapshot to the shared drive
[04:30] Aisha Khan: on encryption, can you outline which data is encrypted at rest and what KMS behaviors are supported? we need to reconcile with our compliance requirements
[04:40] Nora Patel: short answer: model artifacts and KV caches are encrypted at rest; for customer data you can bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) via customer-managed keys in supported clouds; we'll document the key lifecycle and rotation requirements in the security appendix
[05:02] Martin Lowe: sounds good. second topic: marketplace ingestion - what format does Redwood expect for the integration package?
[05:12] Priya Rao: the typical package is: 1) YAML metadata (name, short/long desc, pricing model), 2) quickstart markdown, 3) architecture diagram (SVG/PNG), 4) integration manifest (endpoints, auth methods), 5) screenshots/videos. we'll email a template
[05:35] Sofia Ruiz: any specific auth approaches for the connector? we prefer OAuth in marketplace flows but can support SAML for admin flows
[05:45] Alex Kim: for the connector the standard is mTLS or signed tokens depending on the deployment. for control plane operations we recommend API keys scoped to the integration, and for admin SAML/SSO for the portal access
[06:02] Daniel O'Neal: ok we also need a contact for ingestion bugs - who's the PM on Redwood side?
[06:10] Alex Kim: that's me, Alex Kim, i'll be the listing owner. please cc marketplace@ventracloud in ingestion threads and i'll triage with Priya and Liam
[06:22] Martin Lowe: timeline wise, we'd like the listing in marketplace by mid-october to tie to our product launch. is that feasible?
[06:30] Alex Kim: yes with current asks we can aim for mid-october; next steps are the artifact draft (Alex), security pack (Nora), runbook smoke test (Priya), and VentraCloud providing network/compliance contacts (Martin team)
[06:45] Priya Rao: quick technical deep dive note: for private deployments we recommend an initial staging run in partner VPC with a tiny dedicated GPU pool to validate end-to-end before scaling; we have a standard terraform module and helm charts - we'll share links
[07:05] Sofia Ruiz: terraform module - great. please share repository link, and do you have example values for our registry endpoint?
[07:14] Priya Rao: yes i'll include example values in the repo. link: https://git.redwood.ai/partner/ventracloud-ref-arch (placeholder) and i'll put a short README for common env vars
[07:30] Aisha Khan: a quick clarification on audit logs - we need 12 months of immutable logs for the pilot. can you commit to that retention or will we need to pull logs into our SIEM?
[07:42] Nora Patel: we can provide export hooks to push logs to VentraCloud SIEM; default retention in hosted is 90 days, but for joint customers we can extend retention as part of the private deployment contract. we'll add this to the security appendix
[08:00] Martin Lowe: competitor question - a few customers asked why choose Redwood vs BigCloudAI - do we have a one-liner on differentiation?
[08:08] Alex Kim: short: Redwood is production-first inference with predictable cost controls and unified runtime across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. we emphasize observability and rollout controls (canary, A/B), and clear cost/performance levers
[08:28] Daniel O'Neal: ok good to include in marketplace blurb
[08:35] Martin Lowe: any blockers we foresee?
[08:38] Priya Rao: main technical risk is firewall/NAT rules for the connector and KMS cross-account setup; those are standard and have runbooks. also need to validate our quantization recommended models for some customer workloads - config might need tweaks
[08:55] Alex Kim: suggested mitigation: initial pilot with a single customer in VentraCloud managed VPC, run the perf tests and capture any networking tweaks; build the ref arch doc from that runbook
[09:10] Sofia Ruiz: question about billing: how should usage be reported to VentraCloud customers - do we surface per-token charges or a single partner invoice?
[09:23] Liam Chen: we have flexible billing: marketplace can show per-unit usage to end-customers, and partners can choose revenue share or reseller billing. we'll put options in the commercial appendix of the listing
[09:40] Martin Lowe: great. moving to packaging - can we do a joint solution tile (short blurb + 3 bullets for customers) for the marketplace homepage?
[09:49] Alex Kim: yes we can draft that. action: Alex to provide a 2-line blurb + 3 bullets by 2026-09-03
[09:57] Daniel O'Neal: for the reference arch diagram can you provide layered SVG and a flattened PNG for the marketplace? we prefer SVG for docs and PNG for the tile thumbnail
[10:08] Priya Rao: noted. we'll deliver both
[10:12] Aisha Khan: last security note - for certain regulated customers we may need an air-gapped option; do you have a path for that?
[10:20] Nora Patel: yes we have an on-prem package for air-gapped customers; it requires dedicated ops from both sides, and stronger change control. we'll list it as an advanced deployment option in the listing
[10:35] Martin Lowe: ok let's recap actions and timeline
[10:40] Alex Kim: recap - (1) Alex: draft marketplace listing + screenshots + blurb - due 2026-09-03; (2) Priya: run ref-arch smoke test and upload perf snapshot - due 2026-09-07; (3) Nora: share SOC2/security pack & retention notes - due 2026-09-05; (4) Daniel: confirm ingestion metadata and marketplace owner - due 2026-09-02; (5) Martin: introduce compliance contact if needed - due 2026-09-02; schedule follow-up demo week of 2026-09-13
[11:10] Martin Lowe: thanks all, appreciate the clarity, i'll get my team to pull network specs and compliance contacts.
[11:18] Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc links and draft listing. Alex out
[11:22] (recording ends)
